# Frequently asked questions {#sec-faq .unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: facts
#| include: false
librarian::shelf(dplyr, here, jsonlite, readr, quiet = TRUE)
`%||%`  <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
catalog <- jsonlite::fromJSON(here("data/release/catalog.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
rec     <- jsonlite::fromJSON(here("data/release/datasets.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)
ds      <- readr::read_csv(here("data/release/dataset.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
vers    <- jsonlite::fromJSON(here("data/release/versions.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)$versions
fmt_n   <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
# "1 dataset", "7 datasets"
n_ds_of  <- function(n) paste(n, if (n == 1) "dataset" else "datasets")

n_ds    <- nrow(ds)
n_hold  <- NROW(rec$holdings)
version <- catalog$version
rel_day <- paste(as.integer(format(as.Date(catalog$release_date), "%d")), format(as.Date(catalog$release_date), "%B %Y"))
n_recent <- sum(as.Date(vers$release_date) > as.Date(catalog$release_date) - 90)

# kinds of data: the released datasets' categories, in the catalog's order, as plain words.
# an oxford comma here, since several categories already hold an "and"
cats <- rec$datasets$category
cats <- if (is.data.frame(cats)) cats[order(cats$order), "name"] else unlist(cats)
# lowercase a word's leading capital only, so "Genomics & eDNA" reads "genomics and eDNA"
cats <- unique(gsub("\\b([A-Z])(?=[a-z])", "\\L\\1", gsub(" & ", " and ", cats), perl = TRUE))
kinds <- if (length(cats) < 3) paste(cats, collapse = " and ") else
  paste0(paste(head(cats, -1), collapse = ", "), ", and ", tail(cats, 1))

# licences, by the rule the dataset pages use: an empty licence is unstated, never open
lic   <- ds$license
n_by  <- sum(grepl("^CC-BY", lic %||% ""), na.rm = TRUE)
n_cc0 <- sum(grepl("^CC0", lic), na.rm = TRUE)
n_cus <- sum(lic %in% "custom")
n_non <- sum(is.na(lic) | !nzchar(lic) | lic %in% "unknown")
n_oth <- n_ds - n_by - n_cc0 - n_cus - n_non
```

A word you do not know is probably in the [glossary](glossary.qmd); anything missing here, ask with
the feedback button (the speech bubble beside the light/dark switch).

## What is CalCOFI.io, and how is it different from CalCOFI.org? {#faq-io-org .unnumbered}

[CalCOFI.io](https://calcofi.io) is CalCOFI's data access platform, where you can view data on a map
and download its datasets. The data is updated regularly as new cruise data comes in.
[CalCOFI.org](https://calcofi.org) is CalCOFI's main website. It covers the program's history,
research, sampling methods and news.

Go to CalCOFI.org to learn about CalCOFI, and go to CalCOFI.io to explore and download the data. You
can also get to each from the other: on CalCOFI.org, the
[Visualize data](https://calcofi.org/data/visualize-data/) page under *Data* links to CalCOFI.io,
and every CalCOFI.io page links back to CalCOFI.org in its header.

## What's on CalCOFI.io, and how do the parts fit together? {#faq-parts .unnumbered}

CalCOFI.io has one back end and several ways in. The back end is the **integrated database**: every
dataset CalCOFI has brought in, translated into one shared set of stations, cruises, species and
measurements (see [What does "integrated" mean?](#faq-integrated)). It is published as
**integrated database releases**: dated copies, each with a DOI, never changed once published (see
[Is this the official copy, and how current is it?](#faq-official)). Every way in reads the current
release:

- **[Dataset pages](https://calcofi.io/datasets/)**: one page per dataset, with what it is, who
  collected it, its years, how to cite it, its licence and its download.
- **The [Explorer](https://calcofi.io/explore/)**: one map across every dataset, for one species,
  one measurement, or one area, period, season or depth, with a download of what you choose.
- **[Measurement pages](https://calcofi.io/measurements/)**: one page per measured quantity, such as
  temperature or oxygen, across the datasets that have it.
- **The [R and Python packages](data-access.qmd)**: the same release, read from code.
- **This documentation**: how the integrated database is built and how to use each part.

## How do I download data? {#faq-download .unnumbered}

Go to CalCOFI.io and choose a [dataset](https://calcofi.io/datasets/). **Download** directly from
the dataset's own page. Each download is one zip file holding the data tables, a readme, how to cite
the data, its licence and a dictionary of what every column means.

To get data for a specific area, time period, species or measurement, use the
[Explorer](https://calcofi.io/explore/): choose what, when and where on the map, then press
**Download CSV**.

There are other ways to get the same data. Each dataset page links to the original wherever its
provider publishes it ("Original at …"), for the provider's own version and format. The R and Python
packages read the integrated database release directly from code (see
[Can I get the data in R or Python?](#faq-code)).

## Which datasets are available? {#faq-datasets .unnumbered}

CalCOFI.io has data from CalCOFI's ocean surveys, including `r kinds`. See the
[full dataset list](https://calcofi.io/datasets/) for everything that's available.

The current integrated database release holds `r n_ds` datasets. CalCOFI.io also lists `r n_hold`
more datasets that aren't available for download yet (listed as *holdings*). Their pages tell you
where to find the data. More datasets are added over time.

## Should I use the Explorer or a dataset's page to download data? {#faq-explorer-or-page .unnumbered}

It depends on what you need:

- **Dataset page**: use this to browse a dataset, see an overview, find the original data source, or
  download the full dataset.
- **[Explorer](https://calcofi.io/explore/)**: use this to view data on a map, or to download only
  part of it, such as one region, time period, species or measurement.

## What does "integrated" mean? {#faq-integrated .unnumbered}

Each dataset, as published by its original source, has its own way of recording dates, locations,
species names and units. CalCOFI.io standardizes every dataset into one shared format, with the same
date/time format, station grid (CalCOFI line and station), scientific names (WoRMS, the World
Register of Marine Species; ITIS for birds) and units.

"Integrated" data lets you use datasets together when they overlap in time and place, without your
having to match anything up. For example, fish larvae from a net tow can be matched with a bottle
temperature taken at the same station on the same cruise.

Keep in mind:

- **Depth**: temperature is measured at many depths, while a net tow collects larvae across a range
  of depths. You'll need to choose which temperature to use.
- **Years**: each dataset covers different years. Check each one's date range on its page.
- **Methods**: each dataset uses its own sampling method, so read its page before comparing results.

To use datasets together, use the [Query Builder](https://calcofi.io/query/), or use R or Python
(see the [code packages](data-access.qmd)).

## Is this the official copy, and how current is it? {#faq-official .unnumbered}

Each dataset's official version comes from its original source: every dataset page names the
provider and links the original ("Original at …"). CalCOFI.io holds a copy of them all in
*integrated database releases*. The current release is **`r version`**, published `r rel_day`
(DOI [`r catalog$doi`](https://doi.org/`r catalog$doi`)); a new one comes out whenever the data
change enough to matter, `r if (n_recent == 1) "once" else paste(n_recent, "times")` in the last 90
days. If you know a provider has newer data than a dataset page shows, tell us with the feedback
button. Every release is listed in [Releases](releases.qmd).

## How do I provide feedback on CalCOFI.io and its associated pages? {#faq-feedback .unnumbered}

To report a problem (a value that looks wrong, a broken link, a page that confused you), use the
feedback button on any CalCOFI.io page: the speech bubble at the top, or *Send feedback* at the foot
of the page. It takes a picture of what you are looking at, lets you mark it up, and sends it with
your note to the team. It is also filed as a public issue, so anyone can follow the fix; your email
address is optional and never made public.

## How do I cite the CalCOFI data? {#faq-cite .unnumbered}

Cite two things: each dataset you used (the people who collected it) and the integrated database
release you got it from (the work that put them together). Both citations are on every dataset page
under *Cite*, in every download (the `CITATION` file in the zip), and behind *How to cite* in the
Explorer. The current release's citation is:

> `r catalog$citation`

[Cite this data](cite.qmd) has every dataset's citation and how to cite from R or Python.

## What am I allowed to do with the data? {#faq-licence .unnumbered}

Each dataset has its own licence (its terms for reuse), and they aren't all the same. You'll find it
on the dataset's page and in its download.

In integrated database release `r version`:

```{r}
#| label: licence-list
#| results: asis
lic_rows <- list(
  c(n_by,  "CC BY 4.0",                "reuse freely, with credit."),
  c(n_cc0, "CC0, public domain",       "reuse freely."),
  c(n_cus, "Provider's own terms",     "see the dataset page."),
  c(n_oth, "Another stated licence",   "see the dataset page."),
  c(n_non, "No licence yet",           "ask data@calcofi.io before sharing the data."))
for (r in lic_rows) {
  n <- as.integer(r[1])
  if (n > 0) cat(sprintf("- **%s (%s)**: %s\n", r[2], n_ds_of(n), r[3]))
}
cat("\n")
```

The *Licence* filter on the [list of datasets](https://calcofi.io/datasets/) shows which is which.

## Do I need to sign up or fill in a form to access the data? {#faq-sign-up .unnumbered}

No. Nothing on CalCOFI.io asks you to sign in, register or fill in a form before you look at data or
download it: not the dataset pages, not their downloads, not the Explorer, not the R and Python
packages. If you use the data in a paper, report, app or other product, we encourage you (it is
never required) to register it. That credits the data providers and links your work from
CalCOFI.io. In the Explorer, open *Help* and choose *Register a product*
([how](explore.qmd#sec-explore-help)).

## How do I contribute data? {#faq-contribute .unnumbered}

To contribute a dataset, write to data@calcofi.io; [Providing data to CalCOFI](provide.qmd) says what
a dataset needs and what happens next, including that you see your data on a private copy of the
site and say yes before anything is public.

## Is there a tutorial? {#faq-tutorial .unnumbered}

Yes. The Explorer has a guided tour that walks you through it in the app itself: open *Help* at the
top and choose *Take the tour*, or press `?`. The [Explore](explore.qmd#sec-explore-tour) chapter is
the written version of the tour and follows the same path, with a picture of what you should see at
each stop.

## Can I get the data in R or Python? {#faq-code .unnumbered}

Yes. The `calcofi4r` package for R and `calcofi4py` for Python read the current integrated database
release in a few lines, fetching only the rows you ask for rather than whole files, and `cc_cite()`
in both gives the citations for exactly the datasets you used. Nothing needs a password or an
account. [Access the data](data-access.qmd) shows how, with examples to copy.
